title_original: Liverpool Biennial 2027 theme and artists announced
excerpt_original: The 2027 edition of the Liverpool Biennial will be titled ‘The Age of Magical Thinking’

blocks.alt: Harold Offeh, Hail the New Prophets, 2021
blocks.caption: Harold Offeh, Hail the New Prophets , 2021. Photo: Damian Griffiths. Courtesy Bold Tendencies, London

blocks.text: Aimee Harrison and Lucía Sanromán will curate the 2027 edition of the Liverpool Biennial, titled The Age of Magical Thinking . The exhibition is scheduled to take place from 5 June to 19 September.

The theme draws on psychologist Jean Piaget’s theory of cognitive development, which identified a period in childhood development where imagination is particularly strong. The exhibition will position childhood, a transitional period charged with creative potential, as a lens through which to consider our current global crisis.

‘I think of childhood and youth as a period of constant transition, of change and possibility, but also a time that demands and requires the urgency to question the present’, said Sanromán in a statement. ‘Artists in the exhibition give us insights into the imagination of childhood, spurring us to boldly ask for a better future. The exhibition responds to the loud demands by young people throughout the world to be taken seriously in how political decisions are made, and for whom.’

Ad Minoliti ; Amalia Pica, Anya Paintsil; Charmaine Poh; Dor Guez ; EBB.Global; Elias Nafaa; Francis Alÿs ; Harold Offeh; Hiroko Kubo; Immy Mali; Iván Argote ; the vacuum cleaner; Laakkuluk Williamson; Wen Cheng Lee; Marilyn Boror Bor; Petrit Halilaj ; Rineke Dijkstra; Robert Gabris; Ronak & Roza Moshtaghi; Ruth Ewan; Tania Candani ; Yarema Malashchuk & Roman Khimei ; Zohra Opoku.
